reviews.contract_reason: The pre-fix README promises q conversion for shell quoting and supports Python3.8+. ExecPP.parse_cmd prepares the configured template using info metadata; run passes the resulting string to Popen.run(shell=True). On Windows the old compat_shlex_quote balances literal double quotes but leaves percent expansion; the old Popen runs cmd with delayed expansion off, not percent expansion disabled. A metadata author can therefore cross into a user-authorized exec command when a q-formatted field is used. The earlier de015e930 CVE-2023-40581 helper already uses double-double-quotes and is exactly the same helper text retained at the current parent; the later advisory expressly identifies its percent-expansion bypass. This is old promised argument quoting, not a new exec API or a POSIX claim.

reviews.security_reason: Requires Windows, a user opting into an exec template with q-formatted lower-trust metadata and execution reaching ExecPP. Trusted command configuration is not itself attacker control; the attacker controls a remote metadata value interpreted inside that trusted command. The ordinary cmd setup leaves percent environment-variable substitution effective even with delayed expansion off. The advisory describes command-boundary consequences, but no command, shell, metadata payload, download or exploit executes here. PowerShell as the launching terminal does not change the cmd subprocess used by the retained Windows wrapper.
reviews.negative_reason: After q conversion explicitly calls shell_quote(value, shell=True). Its percent/newline/backslash translation must be paired with the new Windows Popen environment sentinel and /V:OFF /E:ON flags; this is not equivalent to the helper default shell=False mode. The bounded negative is the reported percent-expansion q-field/cmd path under the matched wrapper and ordinary trusted command. It does not certify arbitrary template formatting, missing/default field bypasses, filename fallback, custom executable/shell configurations or universal shell safety. The outer/nested rows are the same changed span; no supported after-contract failure is established for this bounded q path.
